title: Tested companion discs within 11.91 au do not give a 19-year G2874 eclipse
abstract: We test whether a dust disc around an unseen companion can give one continuous 19-year eclipse of G2874. We limit the disc radius to a fraction of the pericenter Hill radius and solve exact Kepler contact times for a finite star. A necessary area for a 0.30-mag fade removes clouds too small to explain the event. In searches over eccentricity and orientation, all 36 main cases have their longest overlap on a circular orbit. At an apocenter of 11.91 au, a full Hill-radius cloud around a 13-Jupiter-mass companion gives 2.193 years, and an 80-Jupiter case gives 3.930 years, for a 0.95-solar-mass primary. Stellar sensitivity tests raise these values to 2.532 and 4.515 years. The circular 13-Jupiter model needs 50.31 au for 19 years, or 80.03 au if the cloud fills half the Hill radius. Slow motion at apocenter does not rescue the tested compact-disc model. The result assumes one continuous eclipse, fixed pericenter-limited dust support, and an orbit within the tested radius. Sparse plates, dust heating, and different infrared epochs do not establish these assumptions. Numerical searches are not a certified global proof. Code, source hashes, checks, and model results are included.

display.caption: Exact circular overlap times and eccentric apocenter transits for pericenter-limited dust support. Stellar mass and radius are each 0.95 solar. Numerical searches find circular orbits give the longest overlaps in the tested cases.
